what_its_for: Avacopan is used to treat a rare disease called ANCA-associated vasculitis (AAV), which causes inflammation that damages small blood vessels in your body. It is used along with other medicines (like rituximab or cyclophosphamide) to help control this disease and reduce damage to your kidneys and other organs.
how_to_take: Swallow the capsules whole with food. Do not crush, chew, or open the capsules. Take avacopan at the same times each day to help you remember. It works best when taken with a meal.
dosing: The usual dose is 3 capsules (30 mg each, for a total of 90 mg) taken TWICE daily with food — once in the morning and once in the evening. Always follow the exact dose your doctor prescribes. Do not change your dose without talking to your doctor first.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If you do not remember until the next day, skip the missed dose and take your next scheduled dose at the regular time. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store avacopan at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct light. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid grapefruit and grapefruit juice while taking avacopan, as they can increase the amount of medicine in your blood and raise your risk of side effects. Tell your doctor and pharmacist about ALL other medicines you take, including over-the-counter drugs and herbal supplements, because many medicines can interact with avacopan (especially antifungals like ketoconazole, seizure medicines, and St. John's Wort). Avoid close contact with people who are sick or have infections, as avacopan can weaken your immune system.
when_to_call_doctor: Contact your doctor right away if you experience: signs of serious infection (fever, chills, cough, painful urination, or wounds that won't heal); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); severe allergic reactions such as rash, hives, swelling of the face or throat, or difficulty breathing; symptoms of hepatitis B reactivation if you have had hepatitis B in the past; or any new or worsening symptoms that concern you.
when_it_works: Avacopan begins working within the first few weeks, but it may take several months before you notice the full benefit. Do not stop taking it on your own even if you feel better — stopping suddenly can cause your disease to flare up. Your doctor will check your blood and urine regularly to monitor how well the medicine is working.
special_populations: Pregnancy: Avacopan may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and for a period of time after stopping. Tell your doctor right away if you become pregnant. Breastfeeding: It is not known if avacopan passes into breast milk. Talk to your doctor before breastfeeding. Liver problems: This medicine is not recommended for people with severe liver disease. Your doctor will check your liver function before and during treatment. Children: Avacopan is currently only approved for use in adults.
